newsitem.title: JAPAN: Japanese police say phoning and driving kills.
newsitem.headline: Japanese police say phoning and driving kills.

text.p: Driving while on the phone in Japan can be hazardous.

Releasing the first statistics of their kind in Japan, the National Police Agency (NPA) said on Friday that nine people died and 1,627 were injured in 1,140 "cell-phone accidents" in the last six months of 1996.
The worst area was Tokyo, which has the largest concentration of cellular-phone users. Drivers in the capital were involved in 86 percent of the accidents.
While cell-phone accidents accounted for less than one percent of all traffic accidents in the same period, the trend was alarming, an NPA spokesman told Reuters.
In a hint of possible similar action, the NPA report stated that five countries -- Switzerland, Italy, Australia, Portugal and Malaysia -- were considering banning drivers from using portable phones.
Telephone companies appear to have woken up to the hazard, starting an advertising campaign calling on drivers to be careful when using the phones.
The NPA report said about half of the accidents happened when drivers were answering a call, one-third while dialling a number and the rest while talking on the phone.
Telephone company statistics show that about one out of five Japanese own a cellular phone, with about 25 million sets in operation.
